findings.title: Exclude successfully scheduled reminders from retry-limit cleanup
findings.body: The retry-count deletion branch also matches reminders with `scheduled: true`. If two invocations load a reminder with retryCount 1, one can successfully schedule it while the other fails and writes retryCount 2. The next invocation then deletes the successfully scheduled future reminder and its Twilio reference, even though the message remains queued externally. This loses the tracking needed to cancel or reschedule that message. Limit retry cleanup to unscheduled SMS reminders and prevent stale failure updates from modifying successfully scheduled rows.

findings.title: Increment retry counts atomically in both failure paths
findings.body: Both failure paths calculate the new count from the snapshot returned by `findMany`. If two cron invocations overlap and both load retryCount 0, two failed scheduling attempts each write 1, losing one failure. A subsequent invocation then attempts scheduling again despite the intended two-failure limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths rather than assigning `reminder.retryCount + 1`.

findings.title: Keep retry bookkeeping failures from aborting the entire batch
findings.body: The new database update inside the per-reminder catch block can itself throw without being caught. For example, another invocation's cleanup can delete a selected reminder while this invocation awaits Twilio. Its first update then fails because the row is missing, and the catch block repeats an update against the same missing row, throwing again. Unlike the previous log-and-continue behavior, this aborts the handler and skips every remaining reminder. Make the retry update tolerant of deleted rows, such as through a conditional `updateMany`, and preserve per-reminder error isolation.
